subset.rationale: ankerl::unordered_dense::map<int,std::string> and set<int> bound HEAD-ON: the library's public alias templates resolve to detail::table<...> specializations, listed explicitly in the reflect_ pack. The query/mutation surface binds directly off the spec -- the non-template at(Key const&)/operator[](Key const&)->__getitem__ (C++ semantics: default-inserts on miss)/erase(Key const&)->size_t, plus the heterogeneous (member-template) contains/count/find, and size/empty/clear/bucket_count/load_factor/max_load_factor as plain methods. Default construction binds via the table() ctor (BINDER-0013 copy-construction also available since table is copyable). The udtest fixture supplies only VALUE-SETTING population (put/add): insert()'s pair<iterator,bool> return has no Python representation (iterators are C++-only) and __getitem__ cannot express assignment. Differential drives the identical lookup/erase/grow scenario through the native oracle and compares sizes, lookup results, default-insert semantics, and erase return codes.
skipped_features: insert/emplace/try_emplace/insert_or_assign from Python (returns pair<iterator,bool>/iterator; iterator types have no Python value semantics -- population via udtest::put/add or d[k] default-insert)
begin/end/find iteration (iterator-returning; a future __iter__/make_iterator feature -- find binds but its iterator return is not value-compared)
segmented_map/segmented_set + PMR variants (same table template, IsSegmented/allocator differ; the standard map/set are the representative head-on bind)
extract/replace/values()/reserve/rehash (value_container_type / node-handle returns with no Python value semantics)
constructors taking bucket_count/Hash/KeyEqual/allocator (defaulted/initializer_list/iterator-range forms have no Python representation; default-construct + populate is the bound path)
